item.title: The next chapter of the 'Asia-Pacific miracle' begins in Shenzhen: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 00:38:00
APEC Illustration: Liu Rui/GT The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. This is China's third time serving as the host of APEC, following the meetings in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. It marks China's most significant piece of home-court diplomacy in the inaugural year of the 15th Five-Year Plan. Leaders and representatives from the 21 APEC member economies will gather in Shenzhen to chart a new blueprint for Asia-Pacific cooperation, centered on the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" and focusing on three key priority areas: openness, innovation, and cooperation. Against the backdrop of accelerating global changes unseen in a century, this major event sends a clear signal to the international community that the Asia-Pacific region is committed to working hand in hand to foster shared prosperity. From the banks of the Huangpu River, the shores of Yanqi Lake to the waterfront of Xiangmi Lake, China has remained in sync with the Asia-Pacific, consistently paving the way and building bridges for regional cooperation. At the 2014 Beijing meeting, China encouraged all parties to overcome long-standing conceptual barriers, leading to the formal adoption of the Roadmap for APEC's Contribution to the Realization of the FTAAP, a document that charted a clear course of action for economic integration. In recent years, despite the rise of unilateralism and protectionism, as well as an increasing tendency to politicize or securitize economic and trade issues, the Asia-Pacific has remained a vibrant hub for cooperation and development. Time and again, events have validated the far-sighted vision China demonstrated back then. Today, as China's relationship with the world undergoes a historic transformation, its role in guiding Asia-Pacific cooperation continues to grow. From development philosophies and rule-making to implementation strategies, China is providing systemic public goods for cooperation across the entire Asia-Pacific region. The shared interests among Asia-Pacific economies have forged stronger bonds of a shared future. China has consistently remained rooted in the Asia-Pacific, contributing to its development and bringing benefits to the region. Today, China possesses both the confidence and the capability to work alongside its Asia-Pacific partners in addressing the defining questions of our time. The region stands at a critical crossroads, where opportunities and challenges intertwine, and many economies are grappling with the test of transformation. Meanwhile, the rapid evolution of digital technologies and the ongoing transition toward a green, low-carbon economy are opening up entirely new avenues for cooperation, fueling an ever-growing demand for the cross-border flow of goods, technologies, talent and capital. As the world's most dynamic economic region with the greatest potential for growth, the Asia-Pacific has unprecedented development opportunities. Now more than ever, it requires interconnectivity to unlock the momentum for sustainable growth. Choosing Shenzhen to host this APEC gathering demonstrates China's dedication to its promises of openness. It allows the world to understand the logic behind China's development in this new era through Shenzhen. The city's transformation from a backward fishing village into a modern international metropolis, characterized by its vibrant innovation and capacity to mobilize global resources, is a vivid example of how openness fosters prosperity and innovation drives growth within the Asia-Pacific region. By hosting the event in Shenzhen, China not only signals its unwavering resolve to advance high-standard opening-up to its Asia-Pacific partners, but also provides a pragmatic platform for all sides to exchange insights on innovation and share development opportunities. Through Shenzhen's experience, economies at various stages of development can discover viable paths forward, allowing the principles of "openness, innovation, and cooperation" rooted in the success story of one city and one nation to evolve into a consensus for development across the entire region. Jointly building an Asia-Pacific community is the original aspiration of Asia-Pacific cooperation and a shared vision among all parties. From the 2013 proposal in Bali to forge an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future, to the 2014 Beijing meeting that launched the process for a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific and outlined a blueprint for connectivity, and continuing with the 2020 "APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040," which set the goal of building an open, dynamic, resilient, and peaceful Asia-Pacific community, China's concepts have consistently resonated with the evolution of Asia-Pacific cooperation. The upcoming Shenzhen meeting will chart a roadmap for realizing this community, establish a framework for collective action among member economies, and yield practical outcomes in areas such as trade, connectivity, the digital economy, and artificial intelligence. As President Xi Jinping has pointed out, the development prospect of our region hinges on the decisions and actions we take today. The APEC Shenzhen Leaders' Declaration is widely anticipated, as are the broader achievements of this APEC "China Year." The Pacific Ocean is vast enough to accommodate the common development of all economies in the Asia-Pacific region. China's own development has benefited from the Asia-Pacific, and in turn, China has contributed to the region's growth and well-being. China accounts for over 60 percent of the region's economic growth and is the largest trading partner for 13 APEC member economies. Committed to openness, innovation and cooperation, China will use the Shenzhen meeting as a springboard to work with all parties toward building an Asia-Pacific community, infusing greater vitality and momentum into the peace and development of both the region and the world at large. Setting out once more from Shenzhen, the great vessel of Asia-Pacific cooperation will surely navigate through the waves toward a bright future of shared prosperity.

item.title: Belgium-Chile alliance in race against China on BBNJ Agreement seen as 'betrayal' of Global South consensus: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 23:45:00
Photo: VCG The surprise announcement by Belgium and Chile to jointly bid to host the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) is unjustifiable, as "it's like a three-way bidding process in which two parties collude to rig the competition," said Zheng Miaozhuang, a researcher at the China Institute for Marine Affairs under the Ministry of Natural Resources. At a regular press conference on November 12, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning flagged six flaws in the joint bid. With only two months left before the first meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the BBNJ Agreement and the vote, the proposal is clearly aimed at closing ranks against the other candidate, China's Xiamen, experts told the Global Times. The experts said the so-called "North-South cooperation" slogan was misleading, calling the move a political deal that undermines fair competition and serves to preserve Western dominance at the expense of the broader Global South. They urged the international community to remain vigilant. Join forces to pressure China In 2025, Belgium nominated Brussels and Chile nominated Valparaiso to host the BBNJ Agreement secretariat. Their sudden announcement of a joint bid has transformed what was originally a three-way race involving Belgium, Chile and China into a "two-against-one" contest, undermining what had been a fair, friendly and transparent competition. "Xiamen has clear advantages in both facilities and supporting infrastructure, putting some pressure on Brussels and Valparaiso," Zhao Chang, an associate research fellow at China Institute for Marine Affairs, told the Global Times. Since China launched its bid for the BBNJ Agreement secretariat, it has received positive responses from the international community, Zhao said. Belgium and Chile each have notable shortcomings compared with China. Chile faces gaps in conference infrastructure, public security, financial support and information and data resources, while Belgium's bid lacks broad support from developing countries. "By announcing their joint bid just two months before the first meeting, Belgium and Chile aim to address their respective weaknesses and combine their strengths, seeking to achieve an effect greater than the sum of their parts. They are also seeking to promote a 'North-South partnership' narrative and win support from both developed and developing countries to increase their chances," Zhao said. The sudden "collaboration" between Belgium and Chile also reflects clear signs of political maneuvering. At the regular press conference on November 12, spokesperson Mao Ning said the joint proposal politicizes the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps. It not only undermines the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of multilateralism, Mao said. "If Xiamen wins the bid to host the BBNJ Agreement secretariat, it would mark the first time a UN body's headquarters is established in China and the first time a UN ocean-related body's headquarters is located in the Asia-Pacific, filling a geographical gap in the distribution of international organizations and helping make global governance fairer, more balanced and inclusive," a source familiar with the matter told the Global Times. This is a scenario some Western countries do not want to see, the source said, adding that they would therefore seek to obstruct China's bid through various means. "The joint bid is not ordinary cooperation between two candidate countries. With the selection of the BBNJ Agreement secretariat entering its final stage, Belgium and Chile are pooling Chile's Latin American representation with Belgium's European diplomatic resources, scientific research databases and experience in hosting international organizations to promote a so-called 'North-South partnership' narrative and win support from more swing countries and regional blocs," Zheng said. Zheng said the move was aimed at pooling the two countries' votes against China and amounted to a joint effort to contain and suppress China's bid, running counter to the Agreement's original purpose and undermining a fair and equitable selection process. Chile's Global South identity reduced to political tool Under their proposal announced by the two countries on November 6, if their joint bid succeeds, the secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement would be based in Valparaiso, Chile, while Brussels would house the base for the treaty's information-exchange mechanism. "Under the proposed division of responsibilities, Valparaiso would nominally take on the secretariat's main functions, while Brussels would retain the physical and technical infrastructure for the clearing-house mechanism and host meetings of subsidiary bodies. On the surface, this appears to be a functional division between a developed and a developing country. In reality, however, it means that 'the secretariat is nominally based in a developing country, while key governance nodes remain concentrated in a developed country,'" Zhao said. Zhao said the information-exchange mechanism serves as a key technical hub for the secretariat's support for treaty implementation and international cooperation, handling information collection, benefit-sharing coordination, matching capacity-building needs with available resources, facilitating scientific cooperation and ensuring database connectivity. Although Chile would nominally retain management authority over the mechanism, its day-to-day operations and technical services would rely heavily on resources based in Belgium. This could make it difficult for the secretariat to fully exercise its management authority, effectively leaving the secretariat in Chile while concentrating key resources for daily operations, professional cooperation and future capacity expansion in Belgium, Zhao said. "By taking control of the information-exchange mechanism, Belgium would be able to maintain its dominance in marine data, control data access, technical support and cooperation networks in high seas governance, and exert lasting influence over information flows, resource allocation and agenda-setting, thereby safeguarding its data hegemony," Zhao said. Meanwhile, under the "Belgium-Chile proposal," meetings of subsidiary bodies would also be held in Brussels, a "concession" by Chile to Belgium. "Hosting subsidiary bodies would further attract experts, national representatives, research institutions and social organizations, concentrating more opportunities for professional exchanges and cooperation in Belgium," Zhao said. She noted that the information-exchange mechanism serves as a hub for data consolidation, resource matching and scientific cooperation, while meetings of subsidiary bodies provide an important venue for technical deliberations and rule refinement. With both based in Brussels, Europe would retain influence over the Agreement's future implementation, information flows and allocation of cooperation resources. "Belgium and Chile have disregarded the legal basis established by the Agreement, which stipulates that there shall be one and only one secretariat and one host country, and that the secretariat's location is to be decided by the Conference of the Parties. Their deliberate division of the secretariat's functions raises questions about their true intentions in the bidding process," Zheng said. In the early stages of its bid, Chile linked Valparaiso's candidacy to developing countries' calls for greater geographical balance in the allocation of international institutions, thereby winning support from many developing countries, Zheng noted. Chile's abrupt alliance with Belgium betrays the stance of developing countries. Its carefully cultivated "Global South" narrative will serve largely as a legitimacy cover for the Belgium-Chile proposal, turning into a tool for Western countries to advance their own interests, Zheng said. "Chile is no longer upholding the position of developing countries, nor does it have the willingness or capacity to independently host a Secretariat with its full range of functions," the expert said. Belgium-Chile proposal raises concerns Although Belgium and Chile have continued to promote their joint bid, the proposal has not been discussed with the broader membership of the Agreement. Their behind-the-scenes division and allocation of secretariat functions raise legal questions. The potential impact of the 12,000-kilometer distance and four-hour time difference between Valparaiso and Brussels on the secretariat's operations also remains unclear. "The proposal is likely to significantly increase the secretariat's operating costs and undermine its efficiency," Zheng said. With UN agencies facing tight budgets, the BBNJ Agreement secretariat should follow the principles of lean, efficient and cost-effective operations in its early stages. Splitting its functions between Europe and the Americas would increase operating costs, raise participation expenses for treaty parties, particularly developing countries, and reduce efficiency. Zheng added that under the Agreement, the secretariat is responsible for managing the information-exchange mechanism, which involves extensive data transmission, storage and application and requires timely maintenance and unified management. Given the distance and time difference between Valparaiso and Brussels, the secretariat in Chile would struggle to manage the mechanism effectively. The proposed office premises for the BBNJ secretariat in Xiamen, China. Photo: Fan Wei/Global Times Many parties have also raised concerns over the transparency of the information-exchange mechanism. In contrast to Belgium and Chile's move to effectively add a second host country in a manner that runs counter to international organizational practices, China's bid has been open and transparent, relying on its merits and genuine commitment. "The key difference between China's bid and the Belgium-Chile joint proposal is whether they respect the Agreement and the collective decision-making process of the Conference of the Parties," Zhao said. The expert added that the two countries had bypassed proper bidding procedures by unilaterally bundling arrangements for the secretariat, information-exchange mechanism, financial mechanism and meeting venues for subsidiary bodies without consulting the broader membership. This oversteps the authority of the Conference of the Parties and could undermine open discussions at the first meeting and fair consideration of other bids. Zheng said bids should be fairly evaluated and collectively decided in accordance with the Agreement and its rules of procedure, adding that compliance, transparency and fair competition are essential to turning a host country's capabilities into a public good serving all parties to the Agreement.

item.title: Several Chinese tech firms report no disruption from Nvidia CEO's exit, cite compliant procurement channels and stable orders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 23:05:00
The Nvidia logo is displayed on a smartphone, with the company's former CEO Jensen Huang in the background. Photo: VCG Several Chinese technology companies said on Monday that their operations remained unaffected by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, citing stable orders, established procurement channels and diversified chip partnerships. The responses came as certain foreign media claimed that Huang's resignation could lead to more US restrictions on chip exports to China, leading to hype about potential disruptions to Chinese AI-related companies. Computing equipment purchases are made through established, compliant commercial channels rather than relying on any particular individual, Sharetronic Data Technology, a Shenzhen-listed provider of AI computing services, data storage equipment and smart devices, said on Monday. In response to an investor's question about potential impact from leadership changes at Nvidia, the company said its business was proceeding normally and that it would continue expanding its range of computing solutions, including developing options based on domestic computing technologies, to respond to changes in the supply chain. "The incident is not directly related to the company's current core business and has not affected its operations. The company's production and operations are currently proceeding normally," Zhuhai Bojay Electronics, a manufacturer of automated testing and assembly equipment serving industries including AI computing, consumer electronics and semiconductors, said in response to an investor's inquiry about impact from changes at Nvidia. Hongfucheng, a Shenzhen-listed maker of thermal management and electromagnetic shielding materials, also said that operations remain normal, with existing orders and deliveries proceeding as scheduled. While noting that the matter concerned a third party's internal governance, which it was not in a position to comment on, the company said that "there are no material matters that should be disclosed but have not been disclosed." The company further pointed out that thermal interface materials undergo lengthy and rigorous qualification processes, meaning existing certifications and mass-production records generally would not change immediately following management changes at a customer. However, changes in customer strategy could still affect purchasing decisions, supplier qualification requirements and order allocations. "To date, the resignation of NVIDIA's CEO has had no impact on the company's operations," said Desay SV Automotive, a Chinese automotive electronics supplier specializing in intelligent cockpit and assisted-driving systems. The company noted that it worked with multiple chip suppliers, including Nvidia, Qualcomm and Horizon Robotics, to develop domain controller products for different vehicle models. Shares of several Chinese companies reportedly linked to Nvidia's supply chains fell sharply on Friday, with optical component maker Suzhou TFC Optical Communication and printed circuit board manufacturer Victory Giant Technology each dropping about 10 percent, according to the Securities Times. Several other Chinese companies had previously said their business ties with Nvidia remained unchanged, while domestic computing firms reported no significant fluctuations in Nvidia chip prices. Huang's resignation came amid intense scrutiny over his extramarital affair with a Singapore-based business executive whom some US media reports and officials alleged had links to Chinese intelligence. The Chinese Foreign Ministry has dismissed the "Chinese spy" allegation as "purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China." China's sci-tech progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. "The US should stop fabricating the 'Chinese spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions," she said. Global Times

item.title: PLA's drone family expands as state media details GJ-11's combat capability
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 22:28:00
The GJ-11 stealth drone Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News military channel After the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force released more close-up footage of the GJ-11 stealth drone, Chinese state media CCTV recently offered further analysis of the aircraft. PLA drones have been frequently featured in media coverage recently, drawing growing attention. An expert said the PLA's formidable drone lineup appears to have a division of labor, but each type is actually moving toward multi-function roles, supporting the Air Force's strategic shift toward integrating air and space capabilities as well as coordinating offensive and defensive operations with new-quality combat forces. On Sunday, CCTV's military channel made note of the GJ-11's distinctive shape and large size. Military affairs commentator Zhang Xuefeng said in the report that preliminary estimates put its wingspan at or beyond that of some light fighters, with a takeoff weight over 10 tons. That size boosts range and combat radius, allows a larger weapons bay for more diverse munitions, and supports bigger payloads such as reconnaissance gear, improving overall capability and future upgrade potential. Zhang said that the GJ-11 has already scored a first-round hit in training, noting that the moment its munitions struck the target meant the drone had achieved combat capability. Zhang further explained that the GJ-11 can strike ground and sea targets and carry anti-ship munitions. It has an infrared electro-optical sensor window under its nose, with sensors typically including visible-light, infrared imaging and laser channels. Laser illumination means it can drop laser-guided bombs for greater accuracy. Its weapons bay can also carry loitering munitions to extend strike range, destroying enemy air defense systems beyond their effective detection range, therefore suppressing the enemy's air defense. The GJ-11 is just one of many new members of China's powerful domestic military drone family. CCTV said that in today's new era, as the PLA Air Force's combat system develops, new-quality combat forces such as drones keep advancing. Some models that have been frequently featured in media reports recently have shown advanced performance. Previously unseen footage of the WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drone conducting a deterrence patrol over China's Huangyan Dao in the South China Sea was released by a CCTV program on Thursday. A WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance unmanned aerial vehicle Photo: Screenshot from the military channel of the CCTV News The WZ-7 is 14 meters long with a 22.8-meter wingspan and a distinctive aerodynamic diamond joined-wing layout. It can carry a synthetic aperture radar, high-resolution digital cameras, infrared thermal imaging equipment and electronic reconnaissance suites, giving it all-weather, round-the-clock reconnaissance capabilities. It can fly at altitudes up to 20,000 meters, which previously left Japanese military planes tracking it only able to shoot blurry photos from below, CCTV said. The WZ-8 is China's high-speed drone. Military affairs expert Du Wenlong said it uses a flying-wing layout and a rocket engine, enabling it to reach an altitude of 20,000 meters and a speed of Mach 2. To date, it is the only drone of its kind in the world. The WZ-10 is a domestically developed unmanned electronic reconnaissance aircraft. Mainly used for electronic reconnaissance missions, it is capable of intercepting and locating enemy radar signals, CCTV said. The shipborne variant of the GJ-11, the GJ-21, the PLA's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike drone, uses a tailless flying-wing, blended wing-body layout with internal weapons bays and fuel space. It made its public debut at the September 3, 2025, V-Day parade. In late October, it successfully took off and landed on the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan , another breakthrough in China's amphibious assault ship development, marking the PLA Navy's capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime platforms. The previously mysterious GJ-3A armed reconnaissance drone only made its debut in an Army Day film in August. Along with the WZ-7 and WZ-10, it provides intelligence support to the PLA Army, Navy and Rocket Force. The GJ-3A armed reconnaissance drone, WZ-10 reconnaissance drone and WZ-7 reconnaissance drone together in a split-screen display Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News Wang Yanan, editor-in-chief of Beijing-based Aerospace Knowledge magazine, told the Global Times that the GJ-3A is a medium-altitude, long-endurance UAV. It can be seen as an enhanced and enlarged version of the Wing Loong, with a likely maximum takeoff weight exceeding 6 tons and a payload capacity of over 2 tons. It is not only capable of air-to-ground strikes but also possesses air-to-air combat capabilities. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Monday that while these models appear to have a division of labor, each is actually moving toward multi-function, multi-module and diversified roles. Reconnaissance-strike drones can also conduct effective detection missions, and stealth drones' penetration can be used for both attack and reconnaissance. Various drones can carry different modules for different functions, for example, adding a navigation module for real-time navigation of an area, or providing communications and relay guidance. In future air combat, manned-unmanned coordination may take two forms. One is crewed aircraft controlling drones to attack, detect and guide targets farther away. The other is true air-combat drones, which need highly advanced AI to effectively accompany crewed fighters as genuine unmanned wingmen. But such wingmen are still under development and not yet a reality, Song said. Beyond air combat, Wang added, the precision operational needs of each service are now closely tied to the massive intelligence data generated by drones. As drone applications in joint operations continue to expand, faster data processing and better intelligent algorithms will open unlimited possibilities for unmanned warfare. PLA drones are moving from single platforms toward a system-based operational architecture, showing a clear path for the Air Force's leap from competing in platforms to competing in systems, and for supporting its strategic transition toward integrated air and space, offense and defense, with new-quality combat forces, Song said.

item.title: Xi to hold China-Russia-US summit with Putin, Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 21:59:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG The meeting of the Chinese, Russian and US heads of state in South China's Shenzhen will be the first face-to-face meeting in history involving the top leaders of the three countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on November 19, according to the ministry. Mao said the heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations, which is of groundbreaking significance. Chinese observers told the Global Times that such a trilateral summit will be a pioneering feat in the history of international relations, and it is conducive to safeguarding the fruits of World War II and maintaining global strategic stability. Javed Akhtar, senior editor of Independent News Pakistan, also noted that such a China-hosted trilateral summit demonstrates China's international influence. The summit matters not only to strategic stability among the three sides, but also to global peace. Amid frequent regional turmoil, international solidarity, coordination and regular dialogue are facing headwinds. The meeting will bolster peace advocates worldwide and open a new chapter for global stability and deeper dialogue and cooperation. China is steadily assuming major-country responsibilities and lending vital support to world peace and stability, he said. Historic summit Russia confirmed participation in the summit on Saturday, and Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said such a trilateral summit is "extremely significant" and dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can't be enforced on others, CBS News reported. Washington confirmed Trump's attendance on Friday, and CNBC reported Sunday that the White House signaled the US intention to prioritize talks over nuclear non-proliferation and the Middle East war at the summit. Yang Xiyu, a senior research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, told the Global Times that the trilateral framework formed by China, Russia and the US could exert enormous influence on global politics and the economy. Such influence extends to peace and stability and strategic risk management in the political and security sphere, as well as practical areas including energy security, artificial intelligence, economic supply chains and sustainable development. Strengthened strategic dialogue at the highest level among the three heads of state is expected to guide and boost dialogue and cooperation between the three countries at all levels and in all sectors, Yang believes. Zhang Jiadong, a professor at the Center for American Studies of Fudan University, dismissed the erroneous narrative by some media outlets claiming the summit would "carve out new spheres of influence." China, Russia and the US are at very different development stages and faced with very different challenges and problems; therefore, the agenda and purpose are completely different. A historical comparison is fundamentally flawed, Zhang added. Yang also pushed back against media reports likening the China-Russia-US summit to a "modern-day Yalta Conference," stressing that a defining feature of the Yalta system was that major powers not only determined their relations with one another, but also made arrangements concerning the fate of smaller countries and the international order affecting other nations' interests. The upcoming trilateral summit, by contrast, is neither intended to determine the fate of other countries nor to carve up spheres of influence, Yang noted. Instead, it aims to explore ways to stabilize and improve bilateral ties among the three countries and their overall trilateral relationship based on shared interests, while enhancing strategic stability among major powers to create favorable conditions for addressing pressing global issues. The summit therefore is significant as the three sides seek to stabilize major-country relations, not escalate major-power conflicts, with an eye on strengthening the management of differences and conflict risks through dialogue, rather than further raising such risks, Yang said, adding that if the summit can encourage the three sides to step up dialogue, explore cooperation and uphold global strategic stability, it will serve as an important counterweight to destabilizing factors amid the transition of the international order. Maintaining strategic stability At the Monday press briefing, spokesperson Mao Ning said that China, Russia, and the US are founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of its Security Council. In history, the three countries fought side by side to win the World Anti-Fascist War. Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder important responsibilities to work together in addressing global challenges and promoting world peace and stability. It is in the interest of the three countries to strengthen communication, manage differences and maintain stable relations. This is also the expectation of the international community and is conducive to global stability, dialogue and cooperation, Mao said. Following China's confirmation on Monday, the global media has focused on the agenda and potential outcomes of the summit, with outlets from different regions prioritizing varying topics including nuclear disarmament, the Ukraine crisis and the Korean Peninsula. Yang said that stable major-country relations constitute a key variable underpinning global strategic stability. Longstanding differences cannot be fixed in one meeting, yet the summit is a promising start. It provides strong political momentum for strategic stability among the three sides and carries important implications for global strategic stability. To enhance communication and coordination does not mean the three sides would abandon their stances, but rather identify common ground and take safeguarding global peace and development as their shared responsibility, Yang further noted. The overriding significance of the summit lies not in settling any specific international issue immediately, but in whether the three sides can forge strategic consensus on the basis of shared interests, explore the right way to get along, and bring greater certainty to global strategic stability, the expert stressed.

item.title: GT Voice: India's trade deficit points to deeper manufacturing problems, not China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 20:51:00
China, India Illustration: Xia Qing/GT India's trade deficit with China is drawing fresh scrutiny. Business Standard has projected that the figure could reach $150 billion in fiscal year 2027. In the debate, China's so-called non-tariff barriers have been singled out by some in India as the biggest hurdle for Indian exports. But India may be looking in the wrong place for the causes of its trade imbalance. Where, then, does the imbalance come from? A large part of the answer lies in the different economic structures of the two countries. India's growth has long been driven more by services than by manufacturing, which accounts for only about 13 percent of its GDP. This is also reflected in the composition of its exports to China, which have traditionally included a large share of agricultural products and raw materials. That pattern is beginning to change. Indian exports to China rose almost 40 percent in the five months through August, an analysis of Indian official data shows, with electronics and engineering goods among the biggest drivers. This points to the gradual expansion of India's manufacturing capabilities. But building an industrial base and broadening an export basket take time. Starting from a relatively modest base, India cannot be expected to close the trade gap overnight. A double-digit increase in exports is no small achievement. Rather than judging progress solely by the size of the trade deficit, India should recognize that strengthening its export capacity is a gradual process, and that the recent growth offers grounds for patience. China has never deliberately pursued a trade surplus with India, nor has it deliberately used so-called non-tariff barriers to restrict Indian exports. On the contrary, China welcomes more high-quality Indian products that meet the needs of its market. The task for India is to develop a wider range of products that Chinese consumers and businesses want to buy, rather than unfairly blame China or expect one-sided trade benefits. Ultimately, much will depend on India's own efforts to strengthen its manufacturing base. Strengthening manufacturing does not mean reducing imports from China. India imports a wide range of raw materials, intermediate and capital goods from China, including auto components, electronic parts and mobile phone components. These inputs feed into Indian production, helping manufacturers make finished goods for both domestic consumption and export markets. Chinese imports are therefore an important part of the supply chain supporting India's manufacturing growth and export capacity. More people in India are beginning to recognize this. A more rational view of trade would allow India to make better use of the opportunities before it. The recent double-digit growth in China-India trade points to the complementarity of the two countries' industrial chains. That is a positive development, and the opportunities it creates should not be lost to an outdated fixation on trade deficits. Calls in India for greater access to the Chinese market are themselves a recognition of its importance to Indian exporters. Given the complementarity of their industrial bases, China and India have room to open their markets further to each other's goods and businesses. But openness cannot be a one-way street. India should reconsider its restrictions on Chinese businesses and products, ease market access and create a more welcoming environment for Chinese companies. If it expects greater openness from China, it should be prepared to offer the same in return. China and India are both developing countries, and development is their common ground. As each pursues its own growth, closer economic engagement can create opportunities for both. An irrational fixation on the trade deficit should not be allowed to obstruct that process. Moving beyond such anxiety would be in India's own interests. Ultimately, a stronger manufacturing base and greater use of trade opportunities will do more to narrow India's trade deficit than fixation on the gap itself.

item.title: From 'Shenzhen speed' to humanoid robots: What draws foreign visitors to China's tech hub during APEC?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 20:24:00
A humanoid robot makes coffee in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, on November 16. Photo: Ding Yazhi/ Global Times What foreign visitors come to Shenzhen to see has changed over the past four decades. In the early years of China's reform and opening-up, they came to witness "Shenzhen speed," see factory assembly lines and learn how China's manufacturing sector operated. Later, their attention shifted to Huaqiangbei, the city's mega electronics marketplace. Today, a new attraction has joined their sightseeing lists: AI 6S stores, robot 6S stores, robot-themed streets and a glimpse of how artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of everyday life. During the APEC meetings, the Global Times reporters visited the robot avenue beneath the Galaxy Twin Towers in Shenzhen's Longgang district on Monday, where a range of technologies are now on permanent display. Coffee-making robots, AI-powered eyewear fitting pods, and robotic dogs capable of boxing are among the exhibits spread across more than a dozen robot-themed display units. The world's first robot 6S store and AI 6S store showcase more than 200 devices, around 30 percent of which are making their global debut or entering commercial application for the first time, a staff member told the Global Times. The robot 6S store was bustling with visitors, about 70 percent of them foreigners. Lin Feng, the store manager, said visitors came not only from the Asia-Pacific region but also from around the world. The growing international interest is reflected in a series of visits. In July, 38 foreign teachers from a university in Shenzhen visited the robot-themed area. A delegation of nearly 40 companies, including Morgan Stanley and the Spanish Friendship Association, also visited the AI 6S store, robot 6S store and robot theater. Many foreign visitors want to understand what robots may be capable of in the future and how far the technology has already advanced, Lin said. They have described the robots as "so amazing" and "completely beyond my imagination." On Tuesday during the APEC meeting week, organizers plan to attempt a Guinness World Record title, with 150 robots performing a continuous coordinated movement for one hour. The demonstration aims to showcase China's progress from small-batch robot production to mass manufacturing and coordinated control of large numbers of robots, Lin said. For one Polish tourist visiting the venue, the experience offered a glimpse into the city's technological development. Having previously visited Macao, he said he chose Shenzhen because he wanted to experience a modern city. The tourist said that it was ''worth it'' to see robots that behave like humans. He said he would recommend it to friends back home, summing it up in three words: "Impressive, modern, future." Behind Longgang's growing robot-themed attractions is an industrial ecosystem supported by universities, research institutions and major technology companies. Products are tested in industrial settings before being brought into 6S stores and public spaces, allowing local residents and visitors to interact with, experience and purchase them, a person in charge of the robot-themed area told the Global Times. Longgang is home to more than 13,000 AI and robotics companies, accounting for nearly one-fifth of Shenzhen's total. The district has also opened up 793 application scenarios under its "City + AI" initiative and established a 1-billion-yuan ($150 million) AI industry master fund, according to the avenue's official statement. The model connects government efforts to open up real-world application scenarios with companies' technological capabilities, moving beyond simply attracting investment and projects to turning the city itself into a platform for AI development, the statement said. Ding Ning from the Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society told the Global Times that this approach is consistent with the spirit of openness embodied in the APEC agenda. The current wave of AI development requires not only advances in algorithms and computing power, but also progress across the entire industrial chain, including equipment, materials, core components and chips, Ding said. Relying solely on market forces could slow technological iteration and foster excessive competition in isolated sectors, while early institutional planning and coordination efforts can help ensure more orderly industrial development. With its comprehensive industrial chain, diverse application scenarios and open cooperation policies, Longgang will promote cross-border technological exchanges, project implementation and two-way investment involving small and medium-sized enterprises. It will also leverage the APEC platform to deepen AI industrial cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region and jointly seize opportunities arising from the development of new quality productive forces, Ding said.

item.title: China-Russia-US leaders set to meet, sending a strong political signal: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 14:39:00
The APEC "China Year" logo decoration is seen at Qianhai Stone Park in Shenzhen. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19, 2026. Photo: Xinhua The efforts to foster a new type of major-country relationship mark a new phase in China's major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, featured by proactive leadership and systematic construction. The meeting to be held in Shenzhen is a manifestation of the international community's high recognition of China's image as a stable and responsible major country. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in China's Shenzhen on November 19. This marks the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the leaders of China, Russia, and the US in history. They will engage in an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in relations among major countries, making this a landmark event. The three countries' efforts to stabilize relations among major countries through mutual coordination not only serve as a powerful rebuttal to the outdated narrative that "great powers are inevitably destined for confrontation," but also send a clear message to a turbulent world: International society can certainly, through dialogue and communication, forge a new path for the peaceful coexistence of great powers in this new era of multipolarity. In today's world, no global challenge can be resolved without the participation of major powers. The stability of global industrial and supply chains depends on policy coordination among major economies; the de-escalation of regional conflicts ultimately relies on influential major countries jointly promoting reconciliation and dialogue; and transnational issues such as global development, food security and energy security can easily fall into a deadlock of endless discussion without basic tacit understanding among major countries. Similarly, emerging issues such as climate governance, public health cooperation and global governance on artificial intelligence will struggle to establish universally binding rules of global governance without the coordinated leadership of major countries. China, Russia and the US are all founding members of the UN and permanent members of the Security Council. Historically, these three countries stood shoulder to shoulder to secure victory in the World Anti-Fascist War. In the current situation, they bear the important responsibility of cooperating to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability. The fact that China, Russia and the US will sit down for face-to-face talks once again demonstrates that the head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance. The effort to foster a new type of major-country relationship marks a new phase in China's major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, featured by proactive leadership and systematic construction. The meeting to be held in Shenzhen is a manifestation of the international community's high recognition of China's image as a stable and responsible major country. Under the strategic guidance of head-of-state diplomacy, China-Russia relations have developed in a long-term, healthy, stable and high-quality manner, while China-US and US-Russia relations have also embarked on a path of positive interaction. The growing consensus among all parties to foster mutual trust and manage competition has become a crucial prerequisite for the trilateral meeting to take place. The three heads of state are about to exchange views face-to-face on important issues. This will not only further enhance mutual strategic trust among major powers but also send a strong political signal to the international community regarding the stability of relations among major countries, thereby helping to boost global confidence in world development. On Chinese soil - the most stable and responsible venue - stability, consensus and confidence converge simultaneously. The right timing, favorable conditions, and sound relations have naturally come together. From a longer-term perspective, if China, Russia and the US succeed in charting a new path of peaceful co-existence, the impact will be far-reaching. There are nearly 200 sovereign states in the world; the vast majority hope to enjoy a stable external environment for development and benefit from the dividends of peace brought about by coordination among major countries, rather than taking sides among them. When China, Russia and the US demonstrate through concrete actions that a new type of major-country relations is a viable model for coexistence, more countries will be willing to join the ranks of multilateral cooperation. The old mind-set of dividing the world along the lines of bloc confrontation will naturally and gradually lose its appeal. Over 80 years have passed since the end of World War II and the founding of the UN, and human society is still struggling to find solutions to major issues such as war and peace, regression and progress, and development and security. Whatever answers may emerge, it must be acknowledged that promoting constructive interaction and overall coordination among major countries on the basis of stable relations will help alleviate disputes, curb turmoil and advance cooperation. Based on historical experience and current realities, China opposes "great-power co-governance" but advocates for strengthening coordination and cooperation among major countries. Guided by the goals of reforming and improving global governance and building a community with a shared future for humanity, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world. The underlying principle it upholds is the democratization of international relations. Those who view the trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the US as major countries "carving out new spheres of influence" or establishing a "new Yalta system" clearly hold only a one-sided view of history, ignoring historical patterns. They focus solely on the needs of individual parties while disregarding the overall and comprehensive interests, emphasize only the power aspect of major countries while neglecting their responsibilities. Strengthening communication, managing differences, and stabilizing relations among China, Russia, and the US is in the interests of all three countries, meets the expectations of the international community, and contributes to stabilizing the global situation while promoting dialogue and cooperation. The trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the US cannot resolve all the challenges facing the international community overnight, but it is undoubtedly opening a path toward more positive, rational and sustainable development. At the same time, it offers a promising direction for addressing the fundamental question of "how major countries should coexist."

item.title: Chinese medical team offers free consultations, diabetes screening in Tanzania's Zanzibar
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16 11:03:00
A doctor with the 36th Chinese medical team to Tanzania's Zanzibar gives a lecture on diabetes prevention and management to local residents on Pemba Island, Zanzibar, Tanzania, Nov. 14, 2026. (The 36th Chinese medical team to Tanzania's Zanzibar/Handout via Xinhua) The 36th Chinese medical team to Tanzania's Zanzibar on Saturday provided free medical consultations and diabetes screening to residents of Pemba Island as part of activities marking World Diabetes Day. The team's Pemba branch conducted the outreach at Tironi Community Health Point in Mkoani District, South Pemba Region, as part of China's "100 Medical Teams in 1,000 Villages" program. It combined diabetes awareness education with multidisciplinary medical services to improve healthcare access in underserved communities. During the event, Chinese internal medicine physician He Yanhong educated residents on diabetes risk factors, blood glucose monitoring, healthy diets, physical exercise, medication adherence, and the early identification of complications affecting the eyes, kidneys, and feet. The medical team also provided free blood glucose and blood pressure checks, consultations and basic medicines. Specialists in internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, orthopedics, ear, nose and throat, anesthesiology and radiology attended to residents, offering individual treatment plans and health advice. Haji Bakar Haji, an official from Mkoani district health authorities, said the initiative addressed healthcare challenges facing remote communities, where residents often travel long distances to access medical services and receive follow-up care for chronic illnesses. He said the outreach had raised public awareness of diabetes prevention while reducing the financial burden of seeking medical attention. Wang Shu, deputy leader of the 36th Chinese medical team to Zanzibar and head of its Pemba branch, said the team would continue organizing mobile medical consultations, chronic disease awareness campaigns and training for local healthcare workers. He said the activities aimed to strengthen grassroots healthcare services, improve local capacity to prevent and manage chronic diseases, and deepen China-Tanzania cooperation in the health sector. World Diabetes Day is observed annually on Nov. 14 to raise global awareness about diabetes. This chronic disease occurs when the body cannot produce enough insulin or effectively use the insulin it produces, resulting in elevated blood glucose levels.

item.title: Chinese scientists identify 'fairy circles' in northern China's drylands for the first time and propose how they form
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15 21:43:00
Fairy circles photographed by the research team near Alxa Left Banner, North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Photo: Courtesy of Yu Kailiang Chinese scientists have recently identified fairy circles, unusual ring-shaped patterns with sparse vegetation or bare in centers, for the first time in northern China's arid regions and used phase transition theory from statistical physics to explain how the circles may have formed in these drylands, the Global Times learned from the research group on Sunday. The joint research conducted by the research team led by Yu Guirui, an academician of the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with researchers from the Lanzhou University and Gansu Agricultural University, was published in the international academic journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) on November 11 local time. Found in the arid regions of Namibia and Australia, fairy circles are unusual ring-shaped patterns in which vegetation flourishes around the edges but is sparse or absent in the center. In China, previous fairy circle research had focused largely on coastal salt marshes, with no confirmed existence in arid and semi-arid regions. The research team studied precipitation gradients along the edges of sandy areas and deserts in northern China, used drones to capture high-resolution images and conducted field surveys. They discovered these patterns, formed by hollow rings of shrubs, at the boundaries between shrublands and grasslands. According to Sun Jingyao, first author of the research paper and postdoctoral researcher at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, the discovery marks the first confirmed record of fairy circles in China's arid regions, alongside with the mechanisms behind their formation being identified as well. Challenging conventional explanations that attribute fairy circles to termite activity or biomass-water feedbacks, the study applies phase transition theory to ecology, suggesting that the patterns emerge naturally when ecosystems reach a critical state, Sun said. Sun explained that phase transition theory, a branch of physics, examines abrupt changes in matter as it shifts from one state or phase to another, and the critical behavior associated with these changes. The researchers used mathematical modeling to demonstrate that fairy circles represent a spatially partitioned "metastable state" in which shrubs and grasses coexist amid intense competition for resources. Sun explained that as precipitation increases and competition from grasses intensifies, the centers of shrub patches become bare due to water scarcity, forming hollow spaces. These hollow rings, in turn, help collect water and sustain the survival of the shrubs. Phase transition theory enables researchers to explain fairy circles and look for early warning signs of ecological collapse along desert margins. Yu Kailiang, corresponding author of the research paper and a research fellow at the institute, told the Global Times on Sunday that fairy circles and vegetation patch expansion were previously treated as isolated natural phenomena and studied separately. However, this study links these phenomena through physical principles, demonstrating that seemingly different abrupt ecological shifts are all manifestations of the same underlying organizational mechanism. It also offers a testable framework for identifying spatial warning signs of potential ecosystem collapse, Yu said.
